study.title: Genesis 1: God creates, commands, blesses, and declares good
study.overview: Genesis 1 He presents God as the only Creator of all that is. The chapter not only states that the world came to be by divine action, but shows that God forms chaos in order, establishes distinctions, fills the earth with life and ultimately judges his work as very good. The text culminates in the creation of the human being, who receives the image of God, the blessing of fruiting and the burden of exercising responsible dominion over creation.

outline.title: God creates the light and separates day and night
outline.explanation: The chapter begins with the creation of heaven and earth and with the initial condition of the earth as formless and empty. God acts by his word, bringing light, evaluating it as good and organizing time through the separation between light and darkness.

outline.title: God organizes the heavens, the waters and the dry earth
outline.explanation: In the second and third days, God establishes the expansion, gathers the waters, causes the dry portion to arise and covers the earth with vegetation. Creation goes from a state of disorder to a habitable and fertile space.

outline.title: God establishes luminations and fills heaven and sea of life
outline.explanation: The luminaries are set to distinguish day and night, mark times and illuminate the earth. Then the waters and the heavens receive living creatures, who are blessed to multiply, showing that life depends both on the decree and the blessing of God.

outline.title: God creates animals and the human being, and approves the whole work
outline.explanation: The earth produces living beings according to its species, and then the human being is created in the image of God, man and woman, with a mandate to master, fruitify and care for the earth. The chapter ends with the divine assessment that everything was very good.

study.context: The notes provided highlight that this chapter opens the Genesis account and, by extension, the beginning of the biblical instruction on creation. The text confronts pagan views of the origin of the world, stating that creation is the work of the one God, who orders the universe without going into battle with other deities. The notes also observe that, in the account, the world is presented in an orderly and functional manner, with the land prepared for housing and sustenance.
study.theology: The chapter teaches that God is sovereign, personal, and orders reality by his word. Creation is not born of chance, nor of conflict between gods, but of the free will of God. The repetition that God sees that it is good shows that the material world is not evil in itself; rather, it has value before the Creator. The creation of the human being is the culmination of the chapter: the image of God confers unique dignity on men and women, and the mandate to dominate is not a license for exploitation, but a delegated responsibility. The blessings given to creatures show that fertility and multiplication come from God, not from rites or magical forces. The closure with the statement that everything was very good affirms the harmony of the divine project before the entry of sin.

scholarViews.insight: The note understands that the chapter introduces the Pentateuch teaching Israel that the world was created, ordained and populated by the one true God, and sees the creation of the human being in the image of God as part of God's purpose of sovereign domination and rest.

The note highlights that the light was the first visible reality created and interprets it as a great good and beauty of creation, highlighting that God brings order and manifests its glory through it.

The note states that the expression on the earth formless and empty communicates confusion and disorder, and understands that God first formed the elementary principles of matter before giving him arrangement and distinction.

questions: What changes in the reading of the world when we begin with the affirmation that God, and not chance, is the Creator?
How does the image of God in men and women redefine dignity, work and responsibility over creation?
How can we treat material creation as good, without falling into idolatry or contempt for the physical world?
study.practice: Recognize God's authorship and sovereignty over all creation, cultivating gratitude before the use of the world's resources. Treat people, animals, environment and time as realities received from God and therefore worthy of responsible care. It is also appropriate to review your own works before God, seeking that what you do to participate in his order, goodness and purpose.
study.uncertainty: The notes provided are excerpts and therefore some observations of the commentators appear summarized. No historical, linguistic or archaeological data were added that were not supported in the biblical text and notes. The references of the commentators were associated with verses of the chapter according to the notes made available, without extrapolating beyond what was explicitly said.
